{"action":"created","issue":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/astropy/astropy/issues/15351","repository_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/astropy/astropy","labels_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/astropy/astropy/issues/15351/labels{/name}","comments_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/astropy/astropy/issues/15351/comments","events_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/astropy/astropy/issues/15351/events","html_url":"https://github.com/astropy/astropy/issues/15351","id":1903203286,"node_id":"I_kwDOAB_CCc5xcJPW","number":15351,"title":"Cannot build `astropy` in CI for exotic archs","user":{"login":"WilliamJamieson","id":20687711,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjIwNjg3NzEx","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/20687711?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson","html_url":"https://github.com/WilliamJamieson","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/received_events","type":"User","site_admin":false},"labels":[],"state":"open","locked":false,"assignee":null,"assignees":[],"milestone":null,"comments":2,"created_at":"2023-09-19T15:07:48Z","updated_at":"2023-09-19T15:41:37Z","closed_at":null,"author_association":"CONTRIBUTOR","active_lock_reason":null,"body":"This issue is related to and referenced by #15333, but it is a separate issue from the general wheel building which was fixed by #15339.

Last week (2023-09-11), all of the weekly cron CI's "exotic" arch tests succeeded:  https://github.com/astropy/astropy/actions/runs/6142559584. However this week (2023-09-18) we got failures in the:

- s390x
- ppc64Ie
- armv7 (32bit)

tests: https://github.com/astropy/astropy/actions/runs/6218804937.

The failures are due to failure to even create the build environment for building the `astropy` wheel to test rather than failures in `astropy` itself. It appears the issue stems from a combination of the changes from #14949 and the release of `numpy` 1.26.

PR #14949 made the minimum numpy needed to build (not run) the astropy wheel 1.25. This means that `numpy` 1.25+ is needed in order to build the astropy wheel in the build environment setup by `pip`. This is posing a problem because prebuilt versions of `numpy` are not available for the archs in question. In particular, we were use the Ubuntu [`python3-numpy`](https://packages.ubuntu.com/lunar/python3-numpy) package installed via `apt-get install` rather than a wheel provided by `pip`. Currently, the latest version of `numpy` provided by Ubuntu (for the lunar version we use in CI) is `numpy` 1.24.2. The reason why #14949 did not cause exotic arch failures when it required `numpy>=1.25` for building `astropy` is because it just so happens that the environment we build in these systems was able to allow `pip` to build `numpy` 1.25 from source as part of creating the build environment for building the `astropy` wheel.

Now that `numpy` 1.26 has been released, `pip` will grab `numpy` 1.26 for the `astropy` build environment (because its the latest version which satisfies our requirements), which also has no pre-builds available for these archs. This is the root of the issue because while our CI happened to have an environment which supported building `numpy` 1.25 it does not support building numpy 1.26.

As we have discussed in previous in #15018, it is preferable for `astropy` to not concern itself with how to build `numpy` in its CI, especially in the exotic archs CI. I believe that this is an entirely reasonable position, especially since `numpy` seems to be shifting its build system around in ways that make it so we have to play constant catch-up in order to continue our exotic arch testing CI. This leads to several possible solutions to this issue:

1. Cease the exotic arch testing on archs which `numpy` does not directly provide a wheel for (so anything that isn't x86_64, aarch64, or arm64).

	- 	This is likely an untenable option, as there are community members who really need us to do this. 

2. Ask numpy to provide prebuilt wheels for the arches we need.

	- 	`numpy` is unlikely to do this just for `astropy`.

3. Ask Ubuntu or Debian to provide packages we can install through their package managers. 

	- 	This might be possible as it has been done for us in the past by @olebole for other packages (on Debian at least).

4. Add some complex logic to https://github.com/astropy/astropy/blob/b9b552a68038f9513616364226a4f98f2c1e0b71/pyproject.toml#L5 in order to select `numpy` < 1.25 (or 1.26) in the archs we are experiencing difficulties with.

	- This is likely possible, but misleading as `astropy` prefers the 1.25 build requirement, see #14915. Moreover, I do not think it is appropriate for `astropy` to do something this drastic just to make CI pass on archs that it does not want to maintain `numpy` building itself on.

5. Revert the #14949 changing the `numpy` requirement for the build environment from `oldest_supported_numpy` to `1.25`.

	- The discussions around #14915 indicate that we would prefer to keep the `1.25` requirement.

6. Pin the `numpy` requirement for the build environment `<1.26`. 

	- I don't think this is a good option as one of our goals for the 1.25 lower pin was that so versions of `astropy` built with this pin should be at least forwards compatible with the `numpy` 2.0 C API.

7. Muddle through and attempt to somehow make our exotic arch environment compatible with building `numpy` from source under these circumstances.

	- As already alluded to, `astropy` does not really want to do this just to support the exotic archs builds as it is a time sink. However, doing this as an interim patch until some other fix for the issue is found.

This solution list is likely not exhaustive so alternate solutions to discuss are welcome.

In any case, I personally don't have much more time to devote to resolving the exotic archs CI failures so I think this issue needs to be opened to the general community to find a tenable (hopefully more long-term) {"action":"created","issue":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/astropy/astropy/issues/15351","repository_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/astropy/astropy","labels_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/astropy/astropy/issues/15351/labels{/name}","comments_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/astropy/astropy/issues/15351/comments","events_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/astropy/astropy/issues/15351/events","html_url":"https://github.com/astropy/astropy/issues/15351","id":1903203286,"node_id":"I_kwDOAB_CCc5xcJPW","number":15351,"title":"Cannot build `astropy` in CI for exotic archs","user":{"login":"WilliamJamieson","id":20687711,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjIwNjg3NzEx","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/20687711?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson","html_url":"https://github.com/WilliamJamieson","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/WilliamJamieson/received_events","type":"User","site_admin":false},"labels":[],"state":"open","locked":false,"assignee":null,"assignees":[],"milestone":null,"comments":4,"created_at":"2023-09-19T15:07:48Z","updated_at":"2023-09-19T19:44:13Z","closed_at":null,"author_association":"CONTRIBUTOR","active_lock_reason":null,"body":"This issue is related to and referenced by #15333, but it is a separate issue from the general wheel building which was fixed by #15339.

Last week (2023-09-11), all of the weekly cron CI's "exotic" arch tests succeeded:  https://github.com/astropy/astropy/actions/runs/6142559584. However this week (2023-09-18) we got failures in the:

- s390x
- ppc64Ie
- armv7 (32bit)

tests: https://github.com/astropy/astropy/actions/runs/6218804937.

The failures are due to failure to even create the build environment for building the `astropy` wheel to test rather than failures in `astropy` itself. It appears the issue stems from a combination of the changes from #14949 and the release of `numpy` 1.26.

PR #14949 made the minimum numpy needed to build (not run) the astropy wheel 1.25. This means that `numpy` 1.25+ is needed in order to build the astropy wheel in the build environment setup by `pip`. This is posing a problem because prebuilt versions of `numpy` are not available for the archs in question. In particular, we were use the Ubuntu [`python3-numpy`](https://packages.ubuntu.com/lunar/python3-numpy) package installed via `apt-get install` rather than a wheel provided by `pip`. Currently, the latest version of `numpy` provided by Ubuntu (for the lunar version we use in CI) is `numpy` 1.24.2. The reason why #14949 did not cause exotic arch failures when it required `numpy>=1.25` for building `astropy` is because it just so happens that the environment we build in these systems was able to allow `pip` to build `numpy` 1.25 from source as part of creating the build environment for building the `astropy` wheel.

Now that `numpy` 1.26 has been released, `pip` will grab `numpy` 1.26 for the `astropy` build environment (because its the latest version which satisfies our requirements), which also has no pre-builds available for these archs. This is the root of the issue because while our CI happened to have an environment which supported building `numpy` 1.25 it does not support building numpy 1.26.

As we have discussed in previous in #15018, it is preferable for `astropy` to not concern itself with how to build `numpy` in its CI, especially in the exotic archs CI. I believe that this is an entirely reasonable position, especially since `numpy` seems to be shifting its build system around in ways that make it so we have to play constant catch-up in order to continue our exotic arch testing CI. This leads to several possible solutions to this issue:

1. Cease the exotic arch testing on archs which `numpy` does not directly provide a wheel for (so anything that isn't x86_64, aarch64, or arm64).

	- 	This is likely an untenable option, as there are community members who really need us to do this. 

2. Ask numpy to provide prebuilt wheels for the arches we need.

	- 	`numpy` is unlikely to do this just for `astropy`.

3. Ask Ubuntu or Debian to provide packages we can install through their package managers. 

	- 	This might be possible as it has been done for us in the past by @olebole for other packages (on Debian at least).

4. Add some complex logic to https://github.com/astropy/astropy/blob/b9b552a68038f9513616364226a4f98f2c1e0b71/pyproject.toml#L5 in order to select `numpy` < 1.25 (or 1.26) in the archs we are experiencing difficulties with.

	- This is likely possible, but misleading as `astropy` prefers the 1.25 build requirement, see #14915. Moreover, I do not think it is appropriate for `astropy` to do something this drastic just to make CI pass on archs that it does not want to maintain `numpy` building itself on.

5. Revert the #14949 changing the `numpy` requirement for the build environment from `oldest_supported_numpy` to `1.25`.

	- The discussions around #14915 indicate that we would prefer to keep the `1.25` requirement.

6. Pin the `numpy` requirement for the build environment `<1.26`. 

	- I don't think this is a good option as one of our goals for the 1.25 lower pin was that so versions of `astropy` built with this pin should be at least forwards compatible with the `numpy` 2.0 C API.

7. Muddle through and attempt to somehow make our exotic arch environment compatible with building `numpy` from source under these circumstances.

	- As already alluded to, `astropy` does not really want to do this just to support the exotic archs builds as it is a time sink. However, doing this as an interim patch until some other fix for the issue is found.

This solution list is likely not exhaustive so alternate solutions to discuss are welcome.

In any case, I personally don't have much more time to devote to resolving the exotic archs CI failures so I think this issue needs to be opened to the general community to find a tenable (hopefully more long-term) Now that #15247 has been merged we may want to consider standardizing the formatting of our `pyproject.toml` file. As noted in https://github.com/astropy/astropy/pull/15247#issuecomment-1713530445 the [`pyproject-fmt`](https://github.com/tox-dev/pyproject-fmt) tool has been created by the tox devs in order to apply consistent formatting to to their `pyproject.toml` files across their various projects.

This PR is applies the `pyproject-fmt` tool to `astropy` and enables its continued use via our `pre-commit`.

Now that #15247 has been merged we may want to consider standardizing the formatting of our `pyproject.toml` file. As noted in https://github.com/astropy/astropy/pull/15247#issuecomment-1713530445 the [`pyproject-fmt`](https://github.com/tox-dev/pyproject-fmt) tool has been created by the tox devs in order to apply consistent formatting to to their `pyproject.toml` files across their various projects.

This PR is applies the `pyproject-fmt` tool to `astropy` and enables its continued use via our `pre-commit`.

Now that #15247 has been merged we may want to consider standardizing the formatting of our `pyproject.toml` file. As noted in https://github.com/astropy/astropy/pull/15247#issuecomment-1713530445 the [`pyproject-fmt`](https://github.com/tox-dev/pyproject-fmt) tool has been created by the tox devs in order to apply consistent formatting to to their `pyproject.toml` files across their various projects.

This PR is applies the `pyproject-fmt` tool to `astropy` and enables its continued use via our `pre-commit`.

Description

Now that #15247 has been merged we may want to consider standardizing the formatting of our `pyproject.toml` file. As noted in https://github.com/astropy/astropy/pull/15247#issuecomment-1713530445 the [`pyproject-fmt`](https://github.com/tox-dev/pyproject-fmt) tool has been created by the tox devs in order to apply consistent formatting to to their `pyproject.toml` files across their various projects.

This PR is applies the `pyproject-fmt` tool to `astropy` and enables its continued use via our `pre-commit`.

Description

Now that #15247 has been merged we may want to consider standardizing the formatting of our `pyproject.toml` file. As noted in https://github.com/astropy/astropy/pull/15247#issuecomment-1713530445 the [`pyproject-fmt`](https://github.com/tox-dev/pyproject-fmt) tool has been created by the tox devs in order to apply consistent formatting to to their `pyproject.toml` files across their various projects.

This PR is applies the `pyproject-fmt` tool to `astropy` and enables its continued use via our `pre-commit`.

"When converting units to strings, the order of the base units is now always the same as it is in the unit itself: by decreasing power to which the unit is raised, and then alphabetical. This avoids super-ugly representations such as `beam-1 Jy` (such as could happen for FITS; see #13217).

However, as can be seen from the PR, it also means some (doc)tests had to be adapted, and it can reasonably be foreseen that this will cause similar down-stream failures. ~Hence, opening as draft for now.~ EDIT: given initial positive feedback, changed to regular PR.

1. The hook would fail to install due to the `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` file not containing a `list` and instead being a `dict`.
2. `repo-review` would fail to run if it was passed all the individual files, which is the default behavior of `pre-commit`.
